text:
To: All Staff
From: Tomas Wieland, IT Security
Subject: Remote access

From 1 November, access to the company network from outside the office will require two-step authentication. The change follows a security review which found that password-only access exposed sensitive client files. [1] Staff who have not yet registered a device of this kind should do so by 24 October; [2] they will be unable to log in.

Devices shared with family members will not be [3] for registration, even where each user has a separate account. [4] the technical details are set out in the attached guide, the IT helpdesk will hold drop-in sessions on 20 and 22 October.

choices: Authentication will be performed by a code sent to a mobile device registered with the IT department.
Authentication will be performed by a code printed on a card issued in advance by the IT department.
Authentication will be performed by a code sent to a device owned by the IT department.
Authentication was performed by a code sent to a mobile device registered with the IT department.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'a device of this kind', so the previous one must mention a mobile device registered in advance; the others mention a card, a department-owned device, or a past tense.
'Otherwise' states the consequence of not registering by the deadline; the others express result or addition.
A device that is 'eligible for registration' meets the conditions; 'legible' means readable, 'elective' means optional, and 'illegal' means unlawful.
'Although the technical details are set out in the guide' concedes that help exists yet sessions will be held; the others do not fit.

text:
Dear Ms. Andrade,

Further to your interview on 12 June, I am pleased to offer you the post of Laboratory Manager, with effect from 1 September. [1] Your starting salary will be £47,500 per annum, to be reviewed after the probationary period.

You will be required to [2] a medical examination before taking up your duties, as the work involves the handling of hazardous substances. The offer is conditional [3] the receipt of satisfactory references from your two previous employers, [4] we have requested directly.

Yours sincerely,
Cleo Hartmann
Human Resources

choices: The first six months of employment constitute a probationary period, during which either party may end it at short notice.
The first six months of employment constitute a period of training, during which the department will provide regular mentoring.
The final six months of the contract constitute a period of notice, during which either party may end the arrangement.
The first six months of employment were treated as a trial, during which the department provided mentoring.
questions.explanation: The next sentence mentions 'the probationary period', so the previous one must introduce it; only the first does.
One 'undergoes' a medical examination, meaning has it done to oneself; 'undertake' means take on a task, and the others do not fit.
'Which' refers to the references and is the object of 'requested'.
